requirements.text: The intended source is committed and reproducible from a clean checkout; the exact verified commit produced the deployed digest-pinned artifacts.
Static, race, PostgreSQL, browser, Helm, generated-contract, and applicable stateful gates pass on that exact commit with zero hidden skips.
Default-deny networking, DR authority, authenticated immutable backups, safe air-gap input handling, immutable image inputs, and supply-chain gates pass.
Estate-scale UI truth, action search, cancellation, accessibility, Playwright, Node/toolchain, and ADR criteria pass.
Estate-100 and every advertised higher scale rung have retained evidence; telemetry correlates API through agent.
All eight Phase 6 external qualifications pass and protected release approval binds the exact artifacts.
Documentation makes only evidence-backed production, scale, accessibility, Rancher-comparison, cloud, DR, and compliance claims.
If physical interoperability is claimed, all 12 Phase 7 runs and cleanup gates pass on exact Astronomer/Constellation candidates.
`advisor-plans/README.md` records Plan 016 DONE and links the retained evidence index. Archived plans remain immutable historical records.
Inventory matches the frozen deployed APIs, UI offers, catalog and static registries with no omitted names, variants or lifecycle flags.
Every required case has a named functional oracle, exact API sequence, owner and fresh PASS evidence; unsupported claims have verified explicit contracts.
All supported install/update/upgrade/rollback/adopt/remove/recovery paths pass without workaround, and each offering performs its promised job.
Real provider and tenant-isolation cases, persistent operation readback and cleanup pass; environment-blocked cases remain visibly unqualified until completed.
Prior known failure paths have been rerun, including pipeline PUT, interrupted upgrades, native backend routing and restore tracking.
UI/API disagreement and advertised-but-unsupported actions are resolved with Plan 027/026, not hidden from the inventory.
Machine coverage verification fails on any newly offered item without a test. CI retains per-build results, and release evidence references them through Plan 016.
Plan and index are updated to DONE only after all above are satisfied. Until then publish the full denominator and PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN counts, not “all extensions work.”
The frozen runtime inventory contains every exposed application, Tool, provider, preset, transport, extension and Charlie capability with no unmatched entry.
Two independent disposable member clusters pass API estate preflight.
All 174 base rows and every runtime-expanded variant have a terminal result.
Every required result is PASS; no FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_RUN remains.
NOT_SUPPORTED appears only where an explicit product contract says so and its truthful rejection was tested.
Lifecycle, canary, authorization, recovery, durable readback and cleanup dimensions pass independently for each applicable entrypoint.
Both K3d clusters are clean after each ownership-conflicting wave and gone after the campaign; management and unrelated resources remain healthy.
Evidence contains immutable candidate/catalog/chart/image identities and no secrets.
`go test ./scripts/qualify-offerings/... -count=1`, offline false-green tests, browser qualification and `make verify-enterprise VERIFY_SCOPE=all` pass on the final source.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Run `git status --short`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git diff --stat f87b189f..HEAD -- internal/agent internal/observability internal/handler internal/charlie frontend/src/lib deploy/chart scripts/loadtest`.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Re-read the source anchors and relevant active-plan status. Record changes and remove tasks already completed; retain outstanding acceptance gaps.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Read live pod/deployment state, image digests, release revision, readiness, connected cluster count, node utilization, volume usage, and protected config references. Never dump Secrets or unrestricted Helm values to a public log.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Identify the actual source revision of each deployed component. Do not assume the frontend, agent, server and worker share one build merely because the chart version matches.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Create sanitized evidence under `advisor-plans/030-efficiency-evidence/<run-id>/`; keep credential files outside tracked paths with restrictive permissions.

requirements.section: E00 — Capture a reproducible starting point
requirements.text: Record target environment, expected ownership, approved mutations and recovery route for later live work. This plan's historical access does not guarantee access in a future sandbox.

Inventory existing metrics before adding names: HTTP duration/errors, DB pool wait/saturation, queue depth/oldest age, audit/task outbox outcomes, tunnel connectivity, event relay lag, heap/goroutines and resource-search outcomes.
Enable application ServiceMonitors in the intended environment; match Prometheus selectors and allowed network paths. Keep base chart usable without Prometheus CRDs.

Add missing bounded-cardinality metrics for inventory refreshes, Kubernetes LIST/GET/WATCH traffic, cache freshness/sync state, reconnects and observation work duration. Reuse `internal/observability/resource_search_metrics.go` registration/label conventions. No resource names, URLs, tokens or unbounded user IDs in labels.
Aggregate agent measurements through an existing supported telemetry path where possible. Never expose a new public unauthenticated metrics endpoint just to collect per-agent data.
Build a dashboard covering API latency, queues/outboxes, DB waits, agent state freshness, downstream API load and resource consumption. Display scrape absence as missing data, not zero demand.

Make alerts distinguish intentional Flux standby from loss of the active artifact-serving controller. Investigate k3s-specific missing scheduler/controller-manager targets; adjust rules to actual observable components rather than globally suppressing alerts.
Capture 30 minutes of idle baseline plus representative interactive operations. Record scrape gaps and cold-start intervals separately.

requirements.section: E02 — Repair actual Flux resource identities
requirements.text: Add regression fixtures matching the bundled Kustomization and HelmRelease CRDs: map entries with `id` and `v`, four identity fields, empty core group, and empty namespace for cluster-scoped resources.

requirements.section: E02 — Repair actual Flux resource identities
requirements.text: First demonstrate the real-schema regression fails on the current decoder.

requirements.section: E02 — Repair actual Flux resource identities
requirements.text: Decode fields into API version, kind, namespace and name. Validate types, malformed IDs, empty/invalid version, mixed valid/invalid entries and the existing maximum resource bound.

requirements.section: E02 — Repair actual Flux resource identities
requirements.text: Preserve documented total-count semantics, sanitization and readiness behavior; do not infer individual resource health from a count.

requirements.section: E02 — Repair actual Flux resource identities
requirements.text: Verify frontend/API inventory consumers receive correct identities. Remove the fabricated schema fixture rather than supporting it as an undocumented compatibility contract.

Trace Grafana proxy image selection from intended candidate artifact through generated Helm values to deployed pod. Determine whether stale desired config, missing distribution, or both caused the unavailable digest.

Use a digest-pinned image available to every target node. Local imports can remain a documented development mechanism, but must cover all scheduled nodes and survive the intended recreation test; production requires durable artifact distribution.

Trace Charlie pull-secret references, registry audience/scope, credential expiry/refresh, and activation reconciliation. A 401 proves authorization failure, not its precise cause. Repair the supported credential/configuration lifecycle without weakening registry authentication.
Add focused tests for image propagation and pull-secret references; keep credential material redacted in failures and audit output.
Exercise the supported Grafana proxy route with authenticated users and denied users. Exercise a real Charlie request and reconnect; pod readiness alone is insufficient.
Demonstrate safe pod recreation in the test environment can pull the intended images without relying on an accidental old node cache.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Reuse the existing harness; do not replace it with raw authenticated loops or direct DB fixture insertion. It already provisions synthetic agents, tracks audit outcomes and exports JSON/checksums.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Run engineering tiers of 5 and 50 synthetic clusters first, then the existing estate-100 profile when infrastructure permits. Higher tiers are optional capacity exploration until lower tiers pass.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Separately test real agents on at least two adopted members, with 1/10/100 delivery assignments and increasing actual Kubernetes resource counts. Synthetic tunnel responses cannot validate informer memory, LIST reduction or Flux behavior.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Fix hardware, component replicas, image digests, chart values, dataset, workload mix and rate limits for each before/after comparison. Record cold start separately; use 5-minute warmup and at least 30-minute measured windows for optimization comparisons, three repetitions where practical.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Include idle estate, active resource churn, inventory browsing, scoped search, delivery status, multiple panels, two browser tabs, and reconnection bursts.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Record throughput achieved as well as requested; skipped work, stale data and HTTP errors cannot count as efficiency improvements.

requirements.section: E04 — Establish the benchmark before optimizing
requirements.text: Add a report reducer/test for proposed cache metrics and relative before/after criteria if the current report cannot express them. Record all mandatory drills as NOT_RUN until genuinely executed.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Map existing informer ownership, stores, typed fields, metadata-only sources, sync readiness and privilege restrictions. Reuse stores capable of answering the inventory question; identify exact missing fields before adding watchers.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Define a narrow injected read-only snapshot interface in a package that avoids an agent/delivery import cycle. Follow the existing `ControllerProbe` injection pattern. Include per-kind availability, sync/freshness information and version/generation where required.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Wire local embedded and remote agents to the same abstraction, scoped to their actual credentials. Do not broaden RBAC to make caching convenient.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Replace repeated whole-cluster workload/PVC lists with snapshot reads. Add scoped watchers only for missing data; strip unused fields to bound memory. Do not maintain a second full-object copy if a safe immutable projection suffices.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Coalesce concurrent refreshes. Give discovery and compatibility checks a bounded slower refresh policy, with explicit refresh on relevant CRD/controller changes.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Distinguish “absent”, “not authorized”, “not synced”, “disconnected” and “healthy”. A cache read must not manufacture a new observation timestamp for old data.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Handle watch expiration/410, relist, object deletion, absent-then-installed CRDs, privilege changes, startup cancellation and shutdown. Informer resync is not a guarantee of fresh server data; handle watch/relist health explicitly.

requirements.section: E05 — Share observation state instead of repeated inventory scans
requirements.text: Use existing transport cancellation/backpressure patterns. Never block informer callbacks on a disconnected tunnel or let pending changes grow without bound.

requirements.section: E06 — Observe assignments from bounded cached state
requirements.text: Reuse or add narrowly scoped Flux source/reconciler observations keyed by GVR, namespace and name. Choose namespace/project coverage according to actual permissions and measured watcher count.

requirements.section: E06 — Observe assignments from bounded cached state
requirements.text: Replace two direct GETs per assignment per status tick where a synchronized snapshot can answer correctly. Retain bounded, explicit fallback for missing capabilities; do not launch one informer per assignment.

requirements.section: E06 — Observe assignments from bounded cached state
requirements.text: Track dirty assignments on relevant changes, coalesce rapid events, and retain periodic freshness/status resync. Preserve acknowledged checkpoint generation and removal/tombstone semantics.

requirements.section: E06 — Observe assignments from bounded cached state
requirements.text: Bound queues and response work; reconnect storms use jitter and concurrency limits. An overloaded or disconnected cluster cannot monopolize management-plane workers.

requirements.section: E06 — Observe assignments from bounded cached state
requirements.text: Preserve failure states, status normalization, agent mixed-version compatibility and continuous Flux ownership. No dropped mutation/audit intent is acceptable.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Capture request counts, payload bytes, rendering time and memory for cluster list, resource list, delivery inventory and scoped search, using the same data as E04.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Audit existing `liveFallback`, stream reconnection invalidation and paced dispatch before editing. Fix demonstrated duplicate requests or missing invalidations; do not replace live transport wholesale.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Share canonical query keys across panels; retain tenant/cluster/namespace/filter dimensions. Ensure cancellation on scope change and no cache leakage after logout, permission revocation or cluster switching.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Verify inactive views and background tabs do not perform unnecessary polling while healthy streaming is available. If cross-tab coordination is justified by measured cost, specify auth/session isolation and leader failover before implementing it; otherwise keep it deferred.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Preserve server-side paging, totals and search semantics. Apply existing TanStack virtualization only to measured large-table render bottlenecks; retain keyboard accessibility, selection and scroll restoration.

requirements.section: E07 — Optimize only measured frontend hot spots
requirements.text: Test stale/reconnecting indicators, disconnected stream fallback, rapid route changes, two panels sharing one query and denied users.

requirements.section: E08 — Tune DB, workers and tunnels only where profiles justify it
requirements.text: Review DB pool wait, slow-query evidence, queue age, handler duration, tunnel fan-out, goroutine/FD growth and audit/task delivery before altering settings.

requirements.section: E08 — Tune DB, workers and tunnels only where profiles justify it
requirements.text: For each hot spot, record exact files/symbols, measured cause, bounded change and test. Prefer batched reads, bounded fan-out, existing cache invalidation and suitable query plans over extra replicas by default.

requirements.section: E08 — Tune DB, workers and tunnels only where profiles justify it
requirements.text: Evaluate worker concurrency against database capacity and downstream limits. Increasing concurrency must not amplify overload or starve latency-sensitive tasks.

requirements.section: E08 — Tune DB, workers and tunnels only where profiles justify it
requirements.text: Preserve periodic-task leadership, idempotency, transactional outboxes and terminal failure semantics. Separate interactive and background budgets using existing mechanisms where available.

requirements.section: E08 — Tune DB, workers and tunnels only where profiles justify it
requirements.text: Any SQL change goes through query sources/sqlc generation and migration safety gates. Do not add speculative indexes or a second database/cache.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Map exporter release ownership, ServiceMonitors, dashboard labels, baseline dependencies and consumers. Pick one supported owner per intended exporter role.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Update owner intent before removing redundant releases so Flux/product reconciliation does not recreate them. Confirm metric names/labels and queries remain valid; retain reinstall/rollback details.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Measure CPU distributions, RSS/working-set peaks, throttling, startup, reconciliation bursts, connection pools and memory after soak. Separate management components from adopted-cluster agents and observability overhead.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Propose dev/small and production profiles with explicit dataset/cluster/RPS envelope and headroom. Do not globally replace HA production defaults with single-node dev measurements.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Reduce requests incrementally in the test deployment and rerun load. Choose limits with burst behavior in mind; CPU limits can cause throttling despite spare node capacity.

requirements.section: E09 — Consolidate exporters and size from representative demand
requirements.text: Treat source-controller standby as intentional. Multiple replicas on one host do not establish host-loss resilience.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Recheck the existing `charlie-dev-rustfs` service and determine an endpoint reachable from backup/drill Pods; the Compose hostname `rustfs` is not assumed resolvable from k3s. Use a dedicated Astronomer test bucket. Verify required S3, versioning and Object Lock behavior against the actual deployed version before configuring backups. Preserve Charlie buckets and data.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Establish dedicated credential Secret references, retention, encryption/wrapping-key custody and source identity using the existing supported configuration. Record achieved backup age and restore duration; proposed dev targets remain RPO ≤24 hours and RTO ≤2 hours. Off-host storage and production RPO/RTO qualification are deferred.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Configure through the supported management/chart owner. Keep writer and retention/delete credentials separate; include encryption/signing material recovery as required by the existing design.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Run a backup and verify authenticated manifest, objects, encryption and completion evidence. Alert on missing/old backup success and failed restore drills.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Restore into an isolated database/environment with no production endpoints or external notification side effects. Verify schema, expected fixture records, credential decryptability, authentication and representative reads.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Record elapsed restore time and backup age. Verify the drill cannot overwrite the source database, and clean up only its own resources.

requirements.section: E10 — Prove development backups and isolated recovery
requirements.text: Document the development restore procedure and its same-host limitation. Track independent storage and recovery when the management host is lost as deferred production work.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Build an internally consistent candidate and retain source/image/schema/config identities. Use the existing release/deployment workflow; inspect rendered changes before applying.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Deploy to a test estate, then a bounded canary. Preserve previous artifacts and configuration for rollback; account separately for any irreversible schema compatibility change.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Exercise agent disconnect/reconnect, watch expiry, event bursts, slow/unreachable member, server and worker restarts, DB/Redis interruption in isolated fixtures, denied RBAC, stale reads and token rotation/revocation.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Prove one failing member does not block unrelated cluster reads. Check explicit partial results, deadlines, event recovery and conserved audit/operation intent.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Run 30-minute comparison windows and a four-hour steady/churn soak. Run real host/etcd/storage failover only on the native multi-node estate and under its existing authorization; K3d on one host is not independent failure-domain proof.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Verify the user journeys: login, cluster list, resource browsing, workload status, Flux resource inventory, Grafana proxy, Charlie request, backup status and restore evidence.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Promote only within authorized scope. Roll back on new sustained 5xx, missing audit intent, growing queues, freshness breach, OOM, lost authorization isolation or failed critical integration.

requirements.section: E11 — Failure qualification and staged rollout
requirements.text: Publish supported capacity, remaining unknowns, before/after measurements and exact evidence. Feed qualifying artifacts into Plan 016 rather than declaring GA here.

requirements.section: Increment A — safe authoring and review
requirements.text: Populate cluster-backed choices such as StorageClass and existing Secret through read-only public APIs, with free text retained for GitOps-created resources.

requirements.section: Increment A — safe authoring and review
requirements.text: Add dedicated validators for Kubernetes quantities, durations, cron, hostname, CIDR and secret references.
Show additions/removals caused by the chart version separately from operator edits.
Warn when an old value path is absent from the target chart while preserving the user's ability to review and remove it.
Show a target-version default diff and removed-path warnings for catalog App upgrades.
Add remaining privilege, CRD ownership, node/storage capacity, image reachability and external-fixture preflight checks.
Link a completed install to its functional surface and last qualification/canary state.
P10.3 Image presence across clusters (blocked: backend has no image filter; see after.md)
New release candidates use the latest stable selected runtimes and tools, with upstream release discovery and qualification recorded.
CNPG remains the production PostgreSQL manager; supported external PostgreSQL remains an explicit operator choice.
Existing CNPG databases, PVCs, keys, credentials, and backup histories survive ordinary application upgrades.
A fresh, uncached disconnected installation can adopt a cluster, install built-ins, scan workloads, and complete selected catalog operations without public egress.
Authentication, tenant authorization, audit, durable operations, and assignment fencing retain their current security guarantees.
Delivery enum values and generated consumers agree with database constraints.
Every supported list makes progress or reports an explicit bounded compatibility error.
Security findings have enforced gates, review ownership, and scoped risk acceptance.
Supported-browser and database-version claims have retained real evidence.
Domain extraction and orchestration consolidation preserve behavior and have characterization coverage.
Release qualification scope is honest and machine checked; existing release exceptions remain accurately recorded.
Every work package has a source-bound evidence record and a reviewed completion verdict.
Create one isolated branch/worktree per bounded package or compatible PR slice.
Record base commit, owning repository, source hash, dependencies, owner, and evidence location.
Reconcile overlapping existing plans before implementation; do not duplicate completed changes.
Re-run applicable verification after rebases or dependency merges.
Keep generated output changes paired with canonical source changes.
Merge dependent slices in dependency order.
Remove worktrees only after preserving needed uncommitted work and verifying merged state.
Avoid accumulating abandoned validation branches or silently replacing another executor's changes.
Map each new task to an existing residual, an independently completed outcome, or genuinely new work.
Mark an already-satisfied task complete only with current code and applicable evidence.
Link historical evidence as historical; never attribute it to a changed candidate.
Update the advisor index with current execution status without rewriting historical results.
Retain `postgres.mode: cloudNativePG` in the production profile.
Retain `deploy/chart/templates/postgres-cnpg.yaml` and scheduled-backup semantics.
Keep the CNPG operator ownership boundary explicit; do not install, upgrade, or uninstall an existing shared operator as an incidental application action.
Retain externally managed Barman Cloud plugin/ObjectStore credentials and configuration.

Preserve cluster name, storage class, PVC identity, WAL storage, instance count, synchronous-replication policy, service names, and application DSNs unless a reviewed migration explicitly changes them.
Preserve database users, Secret references, certificate trust, connection limits, pool sizing, monitoring, backups, and recovery configuration.
Keep CNPG operator upgrades distinct from PostgreSQL server-major upgrades and Astronomer schema migrations.
Keep logical management backups and encryption-key recovery; they are not replaced by an untested CNPG/PITR configuration.
Keep clean-restore and decryption rehearsals after database/image/migration changes.
Refuse major PostgreSQL upgrades by changing `imageName` on an existing data directory without the supported CNPG procedure.
Treat a restored CNPG cluster as a new controlled recovery target; never enable recovery bootstrap against an initialized live cluster.
Rehearse primary failover and application reconnection with real CNPG when updating its operator, plugins, server major, or connection model.
Record qualified CNPG/PostgreSQL/plugin/extension combinations, including airgap images.

requirements.section: W01 — Follow latest stable across runtimes, dependencies, tools, charts, and images
requirements.text: W01.5 Build all first-party Go tools/binaries, including migrator/key rotation/DR/shell helpers omitted by a simplistic server-only inventory. Test reachable vulnerabilities using the actual build toolchain. Build portion PASS on clean `54763ab3`: all 28 discovered command packages, 58 actual steps and 223 default capacity checks; exact source and VCS metadata independently verified. [Build record](../docs/assurance/technology-guide/w01/integrated-build-54763ab3/README.md). Fresh reachable-vulnerability checking remains OPEN, so this combined task stays unchecked.

requirements.section: W01 — Follow latest stable across runtimes, dependencies, tools, charts, and images
requirements.text: W01.10 Expand automatic update discovery to Helm, manual CLIs, CNPG, Flux, Trivy, built-in apps, Charlie compatibility, dev stack, and supporting repositories. Use custom manager/resolver where Dependabot does not cover an ecosystem.

requirements.section: W01 — Follow latest stable across runtimes, dependencies, tools, charts, and images
requirements.text: W01.13 For each lagging component, either qualify the current stable target or record the specific compatibility blocker. Do not silently preserve the old major as policy.

requirements.section: W01 — Follow latest stable across runtimes, dependencies, tools, charts, and images
requirements.text: W01.14 Add freshness dashboard/report data: selected/upstream version, discovery age, exception age, owner, deadline, and evidence. Fail release preflight if the review is missing/stale; offline release preflight validates the signed resolution record instead of contacting upstream.

requirements.section: W02 — Enforce source security and merge policy, preserve scoped risk acceptance
requirements.text: W02.1 Capture current gosec results using the selected toolchain. Triage HIGH/MED findings by code path and rule; separate true defects, inaccessible/test only code, and documented standard platform behavior.

requirements.section: W02 — Enforce source security and merge policy, preserve scoped risk acceptance
requirements.text: W02.4 Keep full-history redacted Gitleaks, safe checkout credentials, action digest pins, and reviewable allowlists. Test reverted-secret detection with synthetic nonsecret fixture values.

requirements.section: W02 — Enforce source security and merge policy, preserve scoped risk acceptance
requirements.text: W02.10 Validate ruleset/check identity against actual emitted workflow checks, avoiding merge queues or skipped jobs that make required checks impossible. Retain a machine-readable readback of applied settings.

requirements.section: The following SHA256SUMS is supplied by the same unverified archive.
requirements.text: W03.4 Build a closed asset inventory from declared supported chart values/presets and actual renders. Include init containers, sidecars, hooks, operators, jobs, enabled optional profiles, and generated downstream workloads.

requirements.section: The following SHA256SUMS is supplied by the same unverified archive.
requirements.text: W03.6 Extend mirror planning to chart archives/repos, workload image values, catalog source URL, Trivy DB assets, CNPG operator/server/plugin images, Valkey, Dex, Fluent Bit, Charlie assets, DR/shell tools, and selected supported integrations.

requirements.section: The following SHA256SUMS is supplied by the same unverified archive.
requirements.text: W03.11 Include chart values-profile and image inventory digests in the signed catalog BOM. Require complete export inventory; preserve operator overrides through an explicit unqualified/needs-requalification state.

requirements.section: The following SHA256SUMS is supplied by the same unverified archive.
requirements.text: W03.12 Reuse hardened release kit extraction and offline Sigstore verification patterns. Do not invent a second weaker verifier or fetch trust keys during verification.

requirements.section: The following SHA256SUMS is supplied by the same unverified archive.
requirements.text: W03.14 Keep S3 configuration endpoint overrides and discovery explicit; distinguish internal data endpoint from externally reachable presigning endpoint where browser links are used. Qualify RustFS operations, not just an HTTP 200 health check.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.1 Define DB assets: main Trivy DB, Java DB when required, media version/schema, upstream revision/digest, downloaded/updated times, expected next update, authenticity metadata, and allowed maximum age.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.2 Configure internal DB repository locations through canonical typed configuration and signed profiles; preserve public GHCR only for explicitly connected mode.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.3 Implement connected mirror refresh and disconnected export/import using latest published stable DB formats compatible with the selected scanner. Use verification/attestation controls appropriate to upstream DB artifacts; do not invent nonexistent upstream signatures.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.7 Distinguish no findings, stale DB, scan pending, scan failed, database unavailable, Java DB not needed, and upstream mirror unreachable in API/UI.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.13 Test missing chart, missing image, stale DB, wrong DB schema, bad signature, local registry outage, DB mirror outage, management disconnect, and reconnect. Required operations fail/degrade explicitly; previously released local Flux continues reconciling.

requirements.section: W04 — Deliver fresh vulnerability databases offline and prove no public egress
requirements.text: W04.14 Declare optional external cloud/SSO/AI/provider features unavailable or separately qualified offline equivalents. Disabling a feature does not qualify that feature as offline.

requirements.text: W11.4 Port one adapter at a time. Preserve existing public operation status and error envelopes; avoid a CLI subprocess replacement that bypasses authorization or durable operation recording.

requirements.text: W11.5 Render the chart across standalone PostgreSQL, CNPG, external PostgreSQL, standalone Valkey, Sentinel, external Valkey, ingress/Gateway, network-policy, and disconnected configurations.

requirements.text: W12.5 Use real databases for transactions, advisory locks, idempotency, JSON constraints, key rotation, outbox ordering, row counts, tenant scope, query plans, and migration compatibility. Keep mocks where they test adapter behavior efficiently.

requirements.section: W12 — Turn support claims into an executable qualification matrix
requirements.text: W12.7 Qualify actual CNPG: three production-mode instances, failover under writes, application reconnect, replicated state, operator/Barman plugin compatibility, physical backup, restore to a fresh cluster, and PITR when claimed.

requirements.section: W12 — Turn support claims into an executable qualification matrix
requirements.text: W12.8 Verify recovery of encryption master keys, key IDs, agent/Charlie credentials, tenant identity, audit chains, and delivery generations. A PostgreSQL restore without the ability to decrypt stored credentials is incomplete.

requirements.section: W12 — Turn support claims into an executable qualification matrix
requirements.text: W12.10 Add Firefox and WebKit projects for critical authenticated workflows and responsive layouts; install matching browser binaries in CI. Keep Chromium route/visual breadth where appropriate.

requirements.text: W12.13 Expand Kubernetes qualification to current stable 1.37 and maintain the declared older range only where actually tested. Include 1.36 as a transition lane and verify kubectl/client-go/Flux/CNPG version-skew support from upstream.

requirements.section: W12 — Turn support claims into an executable qualification matrix
requirements.text: W12.14 Reuse two-cluster and offerings inventories from Plans 028–029 instead of inventing another incomplete list. Verify optional Charlie/provider features only when their services are available.

requirements.section: W14 — Replace fragile operational shell state machines with typed orchestration
requirements.text: W14.1 Classify scripts as small wrapper, fixture generator, developer workflow, release state machine, or runtime operation. Prioritize scripts owning destructive cleanup, secrets, or upgrade rollback.

requirements.text: W14.2 Document inputs, outputs, command compatibility, exit codes, preflight, timeouts, process ownership, evidence files, cleanup and resume behavior before rewriting.

requirements.text: W14.3 Add failure-injection characterization: dependency unavailable, child crash, timeout, signal, partial install, lost lock, cancelled run, interrupted upgrade, and failed rollback.

requirements.text: W14.4 Implement typed plans and bounded subprocess execution with explicit argv/env handling, cancellation, captured exit status, redaction, and resource ownership.

requirements.section: W14 — Replace fragile operational shell state machines with typed orchestration
requirements.text: W14.5 Use durable checkpoints for multi-stage operations that need resume. Separate validation, preview, execution, observation, rollback assessment, and cleanup.

requirements.section: W14 — Replace fragile operational shell state machines with typed orchestration

requirements.text: W15.1 Record catalog build inputs, schema validators, generated outputs, signing/publication ownership, tests, Python scripts, and transitive dependencies.

requirements.section: W15 — Modernize the catalog Python toolchain and supporting repository boundaries
requirements.text: W15.2 Select current stable Python using W01; validate wheels and platform support before changing CI. A release published today may need a recorded short-lived compatibility exception for unavailable dependencies.

requirements.text: W15.4 Define separate runtime/build/test dependency groups; use locked installs and verify regeneration is deterministic.

requirements.text: W15.5 Add Ruff and appropriate type checks, progressing from known interfaces to strict owned modules. Do not hide all errors behind permanent blanket ignores.

requirements.section: W15 — Modernize the catalog Python toolchain and supporting repository boundaries

requirements.section: W15 — Modernize the catalog Python toolchain and supporting repository boundaries
requirements.text: W15.7 Audit dependencies, generate an SBOM, scan generated catalog artifacts, and retain findings/waivers according to the shared policy. Pin GitHub Actions to reviewed commit SHAs with automated update discovery.

requirements.text: W15.8 Verify generated catalog signatures, source metadata, archive membership, image dependencies, and schema versions before Astronomer imports them.

requirements.text: W15.11 Coordinate cross-repository changes with recorded source SHAs and compatible catalog schema versions; test producer/consumer pairs before either side publishes.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.1 Freeze candidate source SHAs across application/catalog/contracts; record chosen versions and scoped exceptions.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.2 Run appropriate focused checks during implementation, then the complete required PR and candidate gates once the integrated candidate is stable.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.3 Build all first-party artifacts with the selected toolchain. Verify SBOMs, vulnerability results, signatures/provenance, declared source SHA, and exact image digests.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.4 Validate the manifest's complete application-image set. The baseline has seven roles: server, worker, frontend, agent, migrate, shell, and DR. Derive required roles from the contract; never hard-code the previous six-image assumption.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.5 Prepare a disposable fresh-install and upgrade rehearsal. Inspect the target context, namespace, current release, CNPG resources, shared operators, PVC ownership, schema, and backup recoverability using sanitized evidence.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.6 Restore a backup to prove database and key recovery before any production-mode major migration. Do not treat an upload confirmation as a restore test.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.7 Deploy the exact signed candidate into local k3s using the supported install/upgrade path. Preserve database CR identity, PVCs, secrets, backup histories, and explicit operator ownership.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.8 Verify browser login/refresh/logout, tenant authorization, durable operation completion, worker recovery, cluster adoption/agent connectivity, Flux generation fencing, built-ins, selected catalog operations, scans/freshness, audit, and telemetry.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.9 Execute the candidate's fresh disconnected qualification with empty caches and blocked public egress. Keep external provider/Charlie requirements explicit.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.10 Compare pre/post deployment IDs, schema, resource ownership, readiness, selected workload outcomes, and customer data invariants without retaining secret values.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.11 Rehearse interrupted upgrade and recovery. The baseline schema is 71 with a declared reversible floor of 66; reread the current contract before execution. Helm rollback must not pretend to reverse an incompatible database migration.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.12 Aggregate machine-readable qualification evidence, exact upstream-CVE waivers, license findings, remaining limitations, and migration notes into the candidate review packet.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.13 Resolve the future tag's actual policy before publication. The approved v1.2.0/v1.2.1 deferrals and absence of a separate named approver apply to those tags; do not manufacture artifacts or silently extend tag-specific exceptions.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.14 Select a future version from the integrated public contract changes. Keep v1 compatibility for ordinary modernization; reserve breaking refactor publication for the separately scoped v2 program.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.15 Publish only after the candidate and applicable approval conditions are satisfied. Preserve v1.2.0/v1.2.1 artifact immutability; fixing a released artifact requires a new version, not overwriting its digest.

requirements.section: W17 — Qualify and release one coherent immutable candidate at each milestone
requirements.text: W17.16 Recheck installed digests and health after publication, preserve the evidence packet, and update completion status only for the scope actually validated.

Include fixes to authentication recovery, malformed durable data, pagination, state parity, catalog trust, freshness reporting, dependency updates, and enforced first-party security gates when their v1 compatibility is proved.
Use expand/migrate/contract rather than deleting old columns, API fields, endpoints, or ciphertext readers prematurely.
Treat raising minimum Kubernetes/browser versions as a customer-facing compatibility decision even if application APIs are unchanged.
Keep PostgreSQL major migration optional and separately rehearsed for existing installations while a fresh-install default is qualified.
Do not block a v1 milestone on optional v2 architecture extraction or unclaimed FIPS capability.
Include accurate migration notes and supported exceptions in each milestone packet.
Validate source/artifact binding, timestamp ordering, expected/actual case counts, result values, required environment fields, and evidence digests.
Distinguish `pass`, `fail`, `not-run`, `deferred`, and `not-applicable`. “Deferred” needs authority/scope; “not applicable” needs a reason.
Sign or attest qualifying evidence when the release contract requires it; merely storing this JSON does not make it signed.
Retain sanitized public summaries separately from restricted raw logs, cluster identifiers, and credentials.
Record reviewer identity and approval separately from machine outcome. Automation cannot invent a human sign-off.
Store manifests and SBOM references by digest so a different rebuild cannot reuse the previous result.

Inventory current Cluster CR UID/name/namespace, operator version and ownership, instance count, PostgreSQL image/digest, extensions, StorageClass/PVCs, replicas, connection routing, ObjectStore/ScheduledBackup resources, key references, and backup retention.
Identify shared resources. Astronomer must not uninstall a shared CNPG operator or Barman plugin during application cleanup.
Confirm current standby/backup readiness and restore actual application state, including decryptable secrets, to an isolated cluster before changing the production path.
Select the upgrade method supported by the chosen stable CNPG release. Use that release's documentation; the moving/development documentation is a research lead, not an executable guarantee.
Separate same-major patching from a major-format upgrade. Do not let a generic image-update bot perform a PostgreSQL major migration.
Rehearse extension compatibility, storage requirements, downtime, application pool reconnect, queued operations, and replica recovery on a copy of representative data.

Prefer an explicitly planned new-cluster/cutover path where it gives clearer recovery. An operator-supported in-place major path needs its own downtime and backup approval; replica PVC recreation may be part of that method, so ordinary-upgrade “preserve every PVC” checks cannot be applied blindly.

Design recovery for post-cutover writes. The old cluster is not a complete rollback source once new writes are acknowledged; define quiescence/replay/restore or accept a measured loss boundary explicitly.

Preserve separate backup/WAL recovery histories across PostgreSQL majors and create a new post-upgrade recovery baseline. Verify selected Barman behavior rather than assuming pre-upgrade archives can recover across the format boundary.
Keep old backups and keys according to retention; verify a chosen restore timestamp lies within the correct major's recovery history.
Compare row counts and representative tenant objects, operation/audit continuity, ciphertext readability, constraints, extensions, indexes/query plans, and worker health after cutover.
Record measured downtime, RPO/RTO, recovery steps and limitations; authorize production migration only after a concrete reviewed rehearsal packet.
Read the candidate's actual schema/rollback floor rather than hard-coding the baseline's 71/66.
Add schema/reader changes first; migrate bounded batches; switch writers only after old/new reader coexistence is proved.
Never run down migrations simply because a Helm release was rolled back. Assess database/application compatibility and recover using the documented safe path.
Back up encrypted data and necessary keys through the supported protected process; retain only references and digests in public evidence.
Restore historical ciphertext with old keys before retiring any reader/algorithm/key.
Reconcile work ownership and outbox state after interruption; avoid replaying a user operation as a new mutation without idempotency protection.
Verify audit linkage and agent/Charlie credential usability after restoration.
Preserve Valkey standalone/Sentinel/external modes and the existing queue/cache semantics. Test Sentinel discovery, authentication/TLS, failover, and worker reconnect where claimed.
Verify supported Valkey upgrades and persisted data compatibility; an ephemeral cache test cannot prove durable queue recovery.
Keep RustFS as the supported in-cluster S3-compatible implementation when configured; keep external S3-compatible endpoints as explicit options. Do not reintroduce a mandatory MinIO dependency.
Verify bucket/object metadata, access control, TLS/CA trust, multipart uploads, retention and recovery semantics used by Barman, catalog kits, scans, and audit/export.
Avoid sharing credentials across tenants or unrelated backup/catalog/scan roles without an explicit threat-model decision.
Check the actual installed RustFS digest and storage layout before changing its version; preserve PVC/data ownership and exercise a recovery test.
Verify every mirrored chart/image/DB asset from its signed inventory and declared trust policy. Rewriting a repository URL does not itself make the rewritten bytes trusted.
Preserve disconnected local Flux reconciliation and last accepted intent even when the management service or upstream registry is unreachable.
Reconcile the operator/agent/Flux/client-go/kubectl/CNPG compatibility matrix before raising cluster minimums.
Use a separate disposable current-stable cluster first; preserve the existing local k3s as a known comparison until the candidate passes.
Treat a Kubernetes minor/major platform upgrade as a platform operation, with its own backup and control-plane recovery; it is not an application Helm update.
Maintain namespace/resource ownership labels and explicit shared-operator boundaries.
Ensure an old agent cannot report stale success or overwrite a new generation after upgrade.
Validate Flux signed-image trust according to its upstream policy; do not replace upstream Flux images with custom forks merely to hide accepted upstream CVEs.
Rehearse cancelled Helm operations and failover during a rollout; compare desired/observed state after recovery.
W00 reconciled source/claim baseline and documented architecture invariants.
W01 selected current stable inventory and exercised discovery/alignment automation.
W02 enforced first-party security gates and transparent scoped exceptions.
W03 verified source-bound catalog/runtime artifacts used by provisioning.
W04 fresh disconnected scans with truthful DB age and imported metadata.
W05 bounded browser refresh, settled queues, cancellation, and form error behavior.
W06 delivery/API/database enums and generated consumers agree.
W07 pagination progresses and stays within authorized scope.
W08 selected fixed SQL is generated with preserved transaction behavior.
W09 durable JSON/request validation and malformed-reader behavior are explicit.
W10 supported observability stack with correlated, redacted signals.
W11 qualified Helm consumer migrations preserving Flux/CNPG ownership.
W12 support matrix has actual current evidence and honest limitations.
W13 v2 preparation has enforced domain boundaries without accidental v1 breaks.
W14 selected operational runners preserve safety and evidence under failure.
W15 catalog tools and supporting version consumers are reproducible and tested.
W17 exact milestone candidate is built, installed, exercised, and recoverable within approved release scope.
All unresolved upstream CVEs/licenses/qualification limitations are disclosed according to the actual applicable policy.
Advisor index and evidence ledger reflect observed status and exact scope.

requirements.section: R06: align system rollout and inventory with intentional warm standby
requirements.text: Fresh supported-cluster run must retain system Kustomization Ready=True beyond the deployment progress deadline, healthy source fetch, application lifecycle, and a negative leader-loss check with recovery. Keep the original demo cluster until R16 passes.

requirements.section: R08: project authoritative Delivery status into Applications
requirements.text: `go test ./internal/handler ./internal/delivery/... -count=1` and applicable real-DB tests pass. R16 browser verifies install→installed and uninstall→removed using the enriched Apps endpoint only.

requirements.section: R10: restore bundle budgets and enforce them in CI
requirements.text: `npm run build && npm run bundle:check` exits 0 with retained fresh byte counts; browser login/configuration/error-path behavior still passes.

requirements.section: R13: restore the frontend dependency audit gate
requirements.text: Select a supported patched dependency or documented source-bound disposition under current policy. Preserve lockfile determinism and editor rendering/sanitization behavior; no global package update.

requirements.section: R13: restore the frontend dependency audit gate
requirements.text: Run high-severity audit, sanitizer negative tests, editor tests, type/lint/build/budgets. A waived gate is not a vulnerability fix; record remaining risk explicitly.

Account for all 32 skips from the current Go gate: unavailable PromQL/chart/signing/private proxy/live OCI fixtures and retired synchronous Dex cases. Qualify required fixtures on the candidate; remove or replace obsolete tests only after their current durable-operation coverage is demonstrated. See the exact skip inventory in implementation evidence.

Diagnose the two operations-pagination full-suite failures using controlled timing/isolation; retain failing runs, root cause and regression. An isolated pass is insufficient closure. Run the full frontend suite once after the fix.

requirements.section: R15: handle the optional Charlie enrollment state
requirements.text: If enabling, obtain fresh enrollment through the supported private workflow and prove readiness plus an authorized action. If retaining disabled, use supported suspend/uninstall semantics with identity retention and no unrelated workload deletion.

requirements.section: R15: handle the optional Charlie enrollment state
requirements.text: Verify bridge endpoints and enrollment readiness match the declared state; never log or retain credential-bearing enrollment bodies in evidence. Provider access remains an explicit dependency.

requirements.section: R16: qualify the actual fixed candidate and retain honest release boundaries
requirements.text: Freeze exact source, images/chart, catalog and supported Kubernetes identities. Run required source gates on that candidate: `make check`, `make security`, changed frontend gates, Helm/distribution and generated-contract checks; retain original outputs and unresolved audit results.

requirements.section: R16: qualify the actual fixed candidate and retain honest release boundaries
requirements.text: Deploy fixes only under a new immutable candidate identity through the supported workflow; preserve rollback material. Do not overwrite released v2.1.1 artifacts or re-label old browser evidence.

requirements.section: R16: qualify the actual fixed candidate and retain honest release boundaries
requirements.text: On the owned supported replacement, require system rollout Ready beyond ten minutes, registration/reconnect, inventory, UI install/configuration/health/uninstall, final durable operation completion, truthful Apps status and desktop/mobile accessibility. Use actual login and supported APIs; no DB status writes.

requirements.section: R16: qualify the actual fixed candidate and retain honest release boundaries

**6.4 Published shared API lifecycle.** v0.1.0 provides `Ensure`, whose `Put` key is the upstream project name and whose create-only result is returned on persistence failure; it does not provide application rotation/deletion APIs. Extend and publish the shared layer's explicit scoped lookup/recovery/revocation contract, with real engine tests and immutable release evidence. Keep engine SDK imports inside the shared library, not Astronomer handlers. Preserve project grants during rotation; record recovery when a create-only secret was lost.

**6.5 Crash-safe registration worker.** Use 6.2 and 6.3 around the shared client; verify stored credentials against returned upstream IDs. Retry `Put` with the original returned Result on persistence failure. Prove timeout after successful write, worker restart, issuer failure, lost database lock and missing secret cases. A process crash before persistence must stop for recovery.

**6.6 Authorized API and configuration.** Add bounded typed provisioning configuration and private administration credentials, explicit project/cluster authorization, transactional mutation audit, operation status and RBAC-safe retries. No provisioning dependency in local login or startup; customer OIDC without shared management capabilities must remain supported as an RP only.

**6.7 Catalog and delivery integration.** Declare supported products and callback contracts, inject issuer/audience/callback plus a scoped Secret reference through the existing delivery path, materialize only to the approved target namespace, and fail closed on incomplete credentials. Keep secret values out of install requests, Helm values, operation responses and audit payloads.

**6.8 Rotation and retirement orchestration.** Stage a new immutable generation, verify consumer rollout before revoking the previous upstream credential, then perform guarded owned Secret cleanup. Track failures durably; uninstall must not delete another installation's app/project or roles.

**6.9 Real product acceptance.** Prove a second supported product's SSO, distinct audience and least-privilege roles; denial for wrong issuer/project; recovery during storage/issuer outages; credential rotation and uninstall. Use deployed candidate artifacts and real browser/API evidence.

**6.10 Release integration.** Qualify private transport/CA, least-privilege provisioning credentials, backup/key recovery, air-gap dependencies, full source/security gates and offering-matrix replacements. Do not mark package 6 complete from adapter tests alone.
